To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deposition mechanism of Cu thin films on functional SAMs surface was systematically investigated using XPS, FESEM and XRD.
the growth mechanism of the CuS thin films is dependent on the surface chemistry and the deposition conditions.
CuS thin films can be grown on the -NH2-terminated self-assembled molecular layer by a CBD technique.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the deposition mechanism and the patterned Cu microarrays on the functionalized SAMs surface.
the deposition mechanism of Cu(2+) ions onto SAMs surfaces and the fabrication of CuS microarrays.
the in situ growth of Cu(2+) and S(2-) in the presence of the -NH( 2)-terminated SAM on the Au substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deposition mechanism of Cu(II) ions on the -NH2-terminated SAMs surface is a combination of ion by ion growth and cluster by cluster deposition in the solution.
the -NH(3)(+) group of the -NH(4)(2+)-terminated SAMs plays a key role for the growth of CuS.
the deposition of Cu(2+) and S(2-) ions in the solution on -NH(3) (+)-terminated SAMs surface can form a complex with the -NH(3)(+)-Cu(2+) bond and then deposit Cu(2+) ions on the surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CuS thin films can be deposited on the functional SAMs surface by CBD.
the growth mechanism of CuS is dependent on the surface terminal groups of the SAMs and the deposition process.
CuS thin films can be successfully deposited on -OH-, -CH(3) and -NH(2) terminated SAMs surfaces by CBD method and the growth of CuS is dependent on the surface terminal groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the functionalized SAMs surface can be used as a substrate to grow CuS thin films and the deposition mechanism of Cu2S thin films on the different functionalized SAMs surfaces can be explained by the combination of ion-by ion growth and cluster-by cluster deposition.
CuS nanocrystallites can be deposited in-situ on the SAMs surfaces using CBD method.
the deposition of Cu2S on -NH(3)(+) functionalized surface can provide a new route to prepare nano-structured CuS films with high electrical conductivity.
